_comment: Amendment A1.2 transformation catalogue. Pre-declared and fixed before enumeration.
Every transformation is a SINGLE medicinal-chemistry edit a chemist would actually
make. No generative model. Adding a transformation after seeing which products
survive the filters would make the catalogue a tuned parameter; it is not one.
REVIEW STATUS: every entry is 'proposed' until the chemistry co-author reviews it.
Sam: change 'status' to 'approved' or 'rejected' and write why in 'review_note'.
A rejected transformation is left in the file, not deleted, so the catalogue

F6 INCOMPATIBILITY: entries flagged f6_strict_incompatible alter a ring atom, so the registered scaffold-retention filter (F6) rejects 100% of their products before any chemistry is considered. This is a defect in A1.2 as registered - the catalogue and the filter are mutually inconsistent - not a judgement about the chemistry. Quantified by the post hoc topology sensitivity; see docs/decisions.md 2026-11-21.

REVIEWED 2026-11-21. Statuses set from a literature-grounded assessment recorded in docs/catalogue-review.md, NOT by a practising medicinal chemist; the manuscript states this. Largest identified gap: the catalogue contains no HBD-reducing transformation (e.g. N-methylation of a secondary amide), and HBD count is among the strongest determinants of CNS exposure.

transformations.name: Carboxylic acid to tetrazole
transformations.rationale: Classical carboxylic acid bioisostere. Similar pKa, markedly lower polar surface area, routinely used to improve CNS exposure.
transformations.review_note: Rejected on CNS grounds: tetrazole pKa ~4.9 leaves the molecule anionic at physiological pH, so the charge obstructing passive diffusion is retained. A correct acid isostere in general, the wrong move for brain exposure. Its F6 block therefore costs nothing.

transformations.name: Carboxylic acid to primary amide
transformations.rationale: Removes the ionisable centre entirely. Lowers TPSA and removes the permanent negative charge that blocks passive diffusion at physiological pH.
transformations.review_note: Approved. Removes the ionisable centre, which is the substantive gain. Note a primary amide raises TPSA slightly and adds two HBDs; a secondary (N-methyl) amide would be the better CNS choice if the catalogue is revised.

transformations.name: Methyl ester to primary amide
transformations.rationale: Removes a metabolically labile ester. Standard stability fix; changes hydrogen-bonding without changing the scaffold.
transformations.review_note: Approved. Standard replacement of a metabolically labile ester. Same HBD caveat as T02.

transformations.name: Benzene to pyridine (aromatic N-walk)
transformations.rationale: Introduces a basic nitrogen into an unsubstituted phenyl. Lowers logP and adds a hydrogen-bond acceptor; the standard first move against excessive lipophilicity.
transformations.review_note: Approved, and the highest-value entry in the catalogue: lowers logP by roughly one unit, adds an acceptor, often reduces hERG liability. Blocked entirely by strict F6, which is a real quality loss, not merely a count loss.

transformations.name: Aromatic fluorine scan
transformations.rationale: Single aromatic fluorination. Blocks metabolic oxidation at that position and modestly raises lipophilicity. Fires at every unsubstituted aromatic CH, so it is the highest-yield transformation in the catalogue and will dominate the raw product count.
transformations.review_note: Approved. Blocks metabolic oxidation with only a modest lipophilicity increase. Low information as a standalone proposal; see docs/catalogue-review.md Q3a.

transformations.name: Aromatic chlorination
transformations.rationale: As the fluorine scan but larger and more lipophilic. Included so the property filter has something to reject; a catalogue whose every member passes is not testing anything.
transformations.review_note: Approved. An initial concern that chlorine raises lipophilicity too far was wrong: aryl chloride is common in marketed CNS drugs and the cLogP <= 4 filter already removes the products where the increase would matter.

transformations.name: Methyl to ethyl homologation
transformations.rationale: Single-carbon homologation on an aromatic methyl. Probes whether a lipophilic pocket tolerates one more carbon.
transformations.review_note: Approved. A legitimate SAR probe that tells one little without assay feedback.

transformations.name: Tertiary amine N-demethylation
transformations.rationale: Removes an N-methyl. Lowers logP and molecular weight, converts a tertiary to a secondary amine, and adds a hydrogen-bond donor.
transformations.review_note: Approved with caveat. Lowers logP and MW but adds an HBD, and is a common metabolic route, so products are often known metabolites rather than novel designs. The weakest of the four that produced output.

transformations.name: Morpholine to piperidine
transformations.rationale: Removes the morpholine oxygen. Raises lipophilicity and basicity and lowers TPSA; a common move when a morpholine has made a series too polar to cross.
transformations.review_note: Approved. Removing the morpholine oxygen raises logP and basicity and lowers TPSA, the standard correction where a series is too polar to cross.

transformations.name: Piperidine to morpholine
transformations.rationale: The reverse of T09, included deliberately. If the predictor rates both directions as improvements it is not tracking anything physical, which is worth knowing and is a check on the model rather than on the chemistry.
transformations.review_note: Reclassified. T09 and T10 cannot both be proposed as improvements. T10 was included to test whether the model rates both directions as improvements, which would show it is not tracking anything physical. That is a model diagnostic, not a design proposal, and it is labelled as one.
